_README: Facts harvested from the live parish site on 2026-08-08. 'status' is the audit verdict against what the Claude Design file asserts. Nothing here is a guess: every VERIFIED entry has a source URL. Entries marked UNVERIFIED stay tagged <!-- TODO: verify --> in the built HTML.

parishName.value: Nativity of the Theotokos Greek Orthodox Church

address.note: Site footer spells it 'Spotswood Furnace Rd'; the contact page body has a typo, 'Spotswood Furnance Road'. Footer spelling used.

fax.note: 2026-08-11 audit asked whether the fax number is unpublished deliberately. This entry carries no such flag either way — unlike `priestCell`, there is no record of the parish asking for it to be withheld. Left unpublished in this pass anyway: deciding WHERE a fax number belongs on the site (the footer already lists address, phone and email without one; contact.html has its own layout) is an editorial decision, not the mechanical marking/recording this issue's other bullets cover, and it is not required by issue #17's verification criteria. Publishing it is a reasonable small follow-up, but should be its own deliberate change.

priestCell.note: Fr. John's personal mobile. It is published on the live parish site and was never rendered into this draft. On 2026-08-09 the parish asked that it be removed from the project completely, so the digits are no longer written down here either — this repository is public, and a number sitting in a data file is published whether or not a page displays it. If the number is ever needed, take it from the parish office, not from this file. NOTE: it remains in this repository's git history; see IMPORT.md.

clergy.title: Presiding Priest
clergy.note: Design's wording matches the live site exactly.

officeHours.note: Design was an hour short. Live site: 'Normal office hours at the church are Tuesday through Friday from 9:00 - 3:00.'

divineLiturgyBook.value: A Greek-English Divine Liturgy book is available — from a greeter, or in the pew. It is not a gift and may not be taken home.
divineLiturgyBook.source: Corrected directly by the parish, 2026-08-08; refined 2026-08-09.
divineLiturgyBook.note: Two corrections, in sequence. The draft first said in six places that a greeter would give a visitor a COMPLIMENTARY prayer book to keep; that was wrong and was changed to 'waiting in the pew'. The parish then clarified that a greeter may well hand one out — what is wrong is the suggestion that it is a gift. Current wording: 'A Greek-English Divine Liturgy book will be available to help you follow the service. One of our greeters will be happy to help you find one.' Both wrong versions are now forbidden patterns in data/site.json, so neither can come back quietly.

sundayServices.note: The design's Visit timeline was right and the live site is misleading: nativity.va.goarch.org shows '9 am Orthros & Divine Liturgy', compressing two distinct services into one 9:00 start. Every place the draft showed a single 9:00 against both services now shows both times. Feast-day Liturgies are NOT covered by this confirmation — the Dormition Liturgy (15 Aug) remains 9:00 a.m. as the design had it, and the 'Great Feasts' line stays tagged TODO: verify.
sundayServices.actionForTheRealSite: The live parish site's own homepage is arguably wrong here. Worth raising separately from this draft — it is the single fact a first-time visitor acts on.
sundayServices.followUp2026_08_09: The last hand-copied list was 'The next few weeks' on parish-life.html, which still dated 14 and 15 August to Thursday and Friday. They are a Friday and a Saturday. It, the month grid on calendar.html and This Week on for-our-parish.html are now all rendered from data/parish-calendar.json, so there is no longer a second copy to correct, or a weekday for anyone to get wrong by hand.

emails.note: Role addresses, not personal ones — safe to publish. 2026-08-13: pctreasurer@ntgoc.org is also the Parish Council Treasurer's card on about.html, confirmed as the right address for that person by the volunteer maintaining this repo. It is filed here under 'stewardship' because that is what the live site uses it for; one address serves both roles.

directions.value: From I-95 take exit 130B and go west on Route 3 for just over 4 miles. After passing the Harrison Crossing Shopping Center (Home Depot), turn right at the next traffic light onto Spotswood Furnace Road and proceed approximately two-tenths of a mile. Riverbend High School will be on the right; the church is on the left, just past the high school.
directions.designSaid: About ten minutes west of I-95, exit 130.
directions.note: Design had the wrong exit (130 vs 130B) and a vague drive time. Replaced with the parish's own directions.

founding.firstLiturgy: 9 April 1989, at St. George's Episcopal Church
founding.charter: 1991, from the Greek Orthodox Archdiocese of North and South America
founding.buildingCompleted: March 2000; first Liturgy in the new church 12 March 2000
founding.note: The design was wrong by 26 years and self-flagged the number as a placeholder. The real history is above. This is the single most valuable correction the harvest produced. 2026-08-11 audit: about.html published only the 1989 first-Liturgy date, even though all four dates carry the same CORRECTED/sourced status. 2026-08-13: the charter (1991), land purchase (1992) and building completion including the first Liturgy in the new church (12 March 2000) are now published in the same caption on about.html, alongside 1989.

paraklesisSchedule.source: Carried over from the design import; not confirmed against a parish source.
paraklesisSchedule.note: 2026-08-11 audit: the 'Regular schedule' panel on calendar.html stated this recurring weekly service with no marker, even though every individual Paraklesis occurrence rendered from data/parish-calendar.json carries `verify: true` and its own TODO: verify marker (see tools/build-parish.mjs). The recurring-schedule line is hand-written, not built from that JSON, so it needed its own marker to match. 'In season' itself is also unconfirmed — which weeks Paraklesis is or is not offered is not recorded anywhere in this project.

confessionSchedule.value: Confession by appointment with Fr. John.
confessionSchedule.source: Carried over from the design import; not confirmed against a parish source.
confessionSchedule.note: 2026-08-11 audit: stated on calendar.html's 'Regular schedule' panel with no marker and no fact entry. 'By appointment' is plausible for a parish this size but has not been confirmed by the parish office, and no other means of arranging confession (e.g. before Saturday Vespers) has been ruled in or out.

metropolis.value: Greek Orthodox Metropolis of New Jersey

feastDay.value: 8 September — the Nativity of the Theotokos
feastDay.source: Fixed date in the Orthodox calendar; also the parish's patronal name.
feastDay.note: Not stated as a date on the live site, but it is a fixed feast, not a parish-specific claim.

ministries.note: Design invented 'Choir & Chanters' (no such ministry page on the live site) and omitted 'JOY' (the younger children's group, which does exist). Both flagged rather than silently swapped — the parish may well have chanters without a ministry page. 2026-08-09: the LIST is settled for this presentation, but the DESCRIPTIONS carried a great deal that was never sourced — meeting frequencies, grade ranges, basketball, retreats, the Metropolis summer camp, named charitable programmes, and September-to-May term dates. All of it is now removed from ministries.html and index.html. Accurate and brief beats polished and invented; see _ministriesNote in data/site.json.

adultEducation.value: Bible studies, catechesis, classes, talks and other opportunities to learn about and grow in the Orthodox faith.
adultEducation.source: Carried over from the design import; not confirmed against a parish source.
adultEducation.note: 2026-08-11 audit: parish-life.html's 'Learning & Formation' section carries a TODO: verify marker with no matching fact entry. Unlike Sunday School (see `sundaySchool`, CONFIRMED_BY_PARISH), no adult-education programme — a Bible study, a catechism class, a speaker series — has been named or confirmed by the parish. The sentence is generic enough that it may simply be true of most parishes, which is exactly why it needs a source rather than an assumption.

prosphoraClass.value: The parish already offers a prosphora baking class.
prosphoraClass.source: Reported by the volunteer who drafted traditions.html, 2026-08-10. Not on the live parish site, not in the newsletter, not otherwise confirmed.
prosphoraClass.note: The single parish claim on traditions.html. Everything else on that page is either a proposal or general Orthodox practice, but this one says the parish DOES something today, and a reader would act on it. Rendered as 'Reported: the parish already offers this class.' with a TODO: verify marker rather than as a plain statement. If the parish confirms it, drop the 'Reported:' framing and the marker together; if it turns out to be a class someone once ran rather than one that runs now, delete the line — 'we used to' is not what the card would be telling people.

traditionsSeries.value: There is no Living the Traditions series.
traditionsSeries.note: traditions.html is an interest survey put together for the Parish Council: twenty-four possible classes, none of them scheduled, approved or staffed. The page carries the same 'Proposed' labelling as welcome.html and states in four separate places that nothing is booked and no form is connected. The class descriptions themselves describe general Orthodox practice (koliva, Vasilopita, palm crosses, Artoklasia) rather than anything specific to this parish, which is why they need no source; where a topic needs authoritative teaching the page says Father would lead or approve it, and names no volunteer as a teacher. Aggregate counts — 'N parishioners are interested in this class' — were requested and deliberately left out: with no form handler, any number displayed would be invented.

coffeeHourHosting.value: Parish households take turns to sponsor the Sunday coffee hour.
coffeeHourHosting.source: Described in the Get Involved brief, 2026-08-10. Nothing on the live parish site and nothing confirmed by the parish.
coffeeHourHosting.note: Plausible — it is what most parishes do — which is exactly why it is tagged rather than assumed. What a host is asked to provide, what the kitchen already has, and what it costs are ALL unsourced, so get-involved.html states none of them and says so in the accordion instead. Those three details are what decides whether somebody who has never hosted feels able to offer, so they are the first thing to get from the parish.

philoptochosCoffeeHour.value: Sun · Aug 16: Philoptochos hosting coffee hour.
philoptochosCoffeeHour.source: Carried over from the design import; not confirmed against a parish source.
philoptochosCoffeeHour.note: 2026-08-11 audit: index.html's upcoming-services list carries a TODO: verify marker on this line but had no matching entry here. Flagging the contradiction it sits next to: `coffeeHourHosting` (below) says coffee hour is sponsored by parish HOUSEHOLDS taking turns, described in the 2026-08-10 Get Involved brief, while this line says a specific ORGANISATION (the Ladies' Philoptochos Society) is hosting on a specific date. Both could be true — a ministry can take a turn like a household does — but neither statement is sourced, and nothing here confirms they are compatible rather than two different pictures of how hosting works. Do not silently pick one; ask the parish which model is accurate, or whether both are.

agapeMeal.value: A monthly parish Agape Meal after the Divine Liturgy, brought by everyone who is able, in place of that Sunday's household-sponsored coffee hour.
agapeMeal.source: Proposed in the Get Involved brief, 2026-08-11. It replaced an earlier and vaguer 'parish potluck on selected Sundays' from the 2026-08-10 brief; neither has been agreed by the parish.
agapeMeal.note: Not another name for coffee hour. Coffee hour is weekly and sponsored by one household; this would be monthly and brought by the whole parish. Keeping the two apart is why 'Agape Meal' stays a forbidden pattern everywhere except get-involved.html — see canonical.forbidden in data/site.json. No date, feast or frequency is published: the card ships with empty rows rather than an invented meal.

theology.mayState: The Eucharist was, at the beginning, celebrated in the setting of a community meal called the agape or love feast; the two became distinct very early, by the end of the first century or the beginning of the second; Christians have gone on sharing a table since, as fellowship and hospitality.
theology.mayNotState: That the Agape Meal completes, extends or forms any part of the Eucharist or the sacrament; or that anyone is expected to eat after the Divine Liturgy. It is a parish supper that remembers an old habit, not a rite, and nobody leaving after Liturgy is leaving early.
theology.grounding: The Archdiocese's account of the sacramental life of the Orthodox Church, as summarised in the brief of 2026-08-11. The specific page URL is NOT recorded in this project and has not been invented; the section names the source in prose instead of linking it. See links.agapeSource in data/site.json.
theology.note: The history is standard and uncontroversial, but it is stated on a parish page over the parish's name, so it stays tagged until someone with the Archdiocese text in front of them confirms the wording. The failure mode is not getting a date wrong — it is a sentence that sounds devout and quietly makes the meal part of the sacrament.

quotation.text: Like our spiritual ancestors in the Church of the First Century, we now come to an Agape Meal.
quotation.speaker: His Eminence Archbishop Elpidophoros of America
quotation.occasion: Remarks following the Divine Liturgy at Holy Trinity Greek Orthodox Cathedral, New Orleans
quotation.source: Supplied in the Get Involved brief, 2026-08-11. No URL is recorded in this project and none has been invented.
quotation.note: A named living hierarch is quoted on a parish page. Of everything on this page it is the item most worth checking against the published text before the draft goes anywhere near the Council: the wording, the occasion and the date. If it cannot be sourced, remove the quotation rather than soften the attribution.

kidsCorner.value: A Kids' Corner during fellowship — books, colouring, quiet play, and occasional activities connected with the saints and feasts.
kidsCorner.source: Described in the Get Involved brief of 2026-08-11 as though it already existed; confirmed by Thomas on 2026-08-11 that it does not.
kidsCorner.note: Written as a proposal on the page for that reason, and matched to the 'Kids' Corner' entry under 'There is a place for you', which is the ministry it would need in order to exist. The page also states that parents remain responsible for their own children and that the corner is not childcare — worth keeping in any rewrite, because an unattended-children expectation is a safeguarding question, not a copy question.

mealMinistry.value: Meals coordinated for a parish household after a birth, illness, surgery or bereavement — offered through a meal train, and requested privately through a parish ministry coordinator.
mealMinistry.source: Proposed in the Get Involved brief, 2026-08-10. No such ministry is named on the live parish site.
mealMinistry.note: Two halves, and the second one carries the risk. OFFERING to cook is public and harmless. ASKING for meals is not: it discloses a birth, an illness, a surgery or a death, so the request route must be private, must reach one named coordinator, and must never create a public Meal Train page by itself. get-involved.html builds the interface and states in the page's own words that nothing is transmitted; it publishes no list of people who have asked, and it must not acquire one. Needs from the parish: who the coordinator is, and a private destination Fr. John has approved.

hallRental.designSaid: Capacity ≈ 200 seated; full commercial kitchen; on-site free parking
hallRental.note: The live hall-rental page gives NO capacity, kitchen, or parking details — only a deposit link and a contract PDF. Every one of the design's three specifics is unsourced. Left in place, each tagged TODO: verify. 2026-08-11 audit: hall.html's introductory paragraph also restated capacity and kitchen (now tagged to match the grid rows below) and separately claimed 'tables and chairs' and 'a sound system' — neither of which is in the design's original three specifics or on the live hall-rental page. Both are plausible for a rentable hall and both are now tagged TODO: verify rather than removed or invented further. 'Its own parking' was reworded to 'parking on site': the parking fact is CONFIRMED_BY_PARISH as free, shared, on-site parking for the whole property (see `parking` below and data/site.json parking.note) — 'its own' overstated that as dedicated hall-only parking, which is not confirmed.

parishCouncil.value: Nine members. Gamal Salem, President; Jason Yianilos, Vice President; Eleni Yiasemides, Treasurer; Nick Roman, Secretary; Dan Athanasaw; Anthony Hatzis; Dennis Makrinos; Chris Papanastasiou; Christopher Rigopoulos.
parishCouncil.source: The parish newsletter's organisation and officer list, supplied 2026-08-13 by the volunteer maintaining this repo. Approved by the Parish Council at a meeting before that date — see _rosterPermission — and the approval covers the list itself, not only the decision to publish it: nine members, those four offices, those spellings. No TODO: verify marker remains on any name.
parishCouncil.designSaid: 7 members named in full, each with an @ntgoc.org address
parishCouncil.supersedes: Until 2026-08-13 this entry read WITHHELD: 'Replaced with neutral placeholders per your instruction. The live site's Parish Council page was not scraped for names.' That instruction is superseded by the parish's decision to publish the roster in the draft (see _rosterPermission below). The withholding was never about these names being secret — the live site simply does not carry them, so there was nothing sourced to publish.
parishCouncil.note: PUBLISHED on about.html, ten cards including Fr. John. Four points on what is and is not asserted. (1) ORDER is officers in office order, then the five remaining members alphabetically by surname — the newsletter's own order is not alphabetical and carries no evident meaning, and an arbitrary order on a page reads as a ranking. (2) The seven invented BIOGRAPHIES are gone, not re-attached. Each said which committee that member co-leads ('Co-leads Building and Grounds', and so on); the newsletter gives no committee assignments, so keeping them would have pinned an unsourced committee role on a named parishioner. Fr. John's biography lost its 'leading the Worship and Liturgical Committee' clause for the same reason. committees.html therefore still reads 'Council Member' for every lead — the roster does not answer the question that page asks. (3) EMAIL is office@ntgoc.org on every card except the Treasurer's, which carries pctreasurer@ntgoc.org. Both are verified role addresses, not personal ones (see emails). The pairing was raised as a question rather than assumed — the local part plainly reads 'parish council treasurer', which is suggestive but is not a source — and confirmed 2026-08-13 by the volunteer maintaining this repo. Note that `emails` files pctreasurer@ntgoc.org under 'stewardship', which is where the live site uses it; the same address serving both is the parish's arrangement, not a contradiction in this file. (4) No personal email address or telephone number was supplied and none is published.

philoptochosBoard.value: Yvonne Athanasaw, President; Maria Yiasemides, Vice President; Christina Turdean, Treasurer; Jane Kalomatis Moore, Assistant Treasurer; Martha Ziegenfuss, Recording Secretary; Yvonne Rigopoulos, Corresponding Secretary; Anthoula Makrinos, Board Member; Lambrini Zourzoukis, Board Member; Verilee Vasilakos, Advisor.
philoptochosBoard.source: The parish newsletter's organisation and officer list, supplied 2026-08-13 by the volunteer maintaining this repo, and covered by the same Parish Council approval as parishCouncil — see _rosterPermission, including the one caveat there about the Council approving a roster that is the Philoptochos's own.
philoptochosBoard.note: PUBLISHED on ministries.html in a new chunk, ntgocPhiloptochosBoard, which is the only place on the site with room for a nine-person board. Ordered officers first (President, Vice President, Treasurer, Assistant Treasurer, then the two secretaries), then board members, then the Advisor — the newsletter's order, with the two treasurers and the two secretaries brought together. Cards carry name and office only: no email address, because office@ntgoc.org reaches the church office rather than the society, and inventing a philoptochos@ address would be worse. The section note says to write to the parish office instead. NOT asserted: that the society is open to any woman of the parish, what it does with what it raises, or when it meets. None of that is sourced. The same person appears here as Assistant Treasurer and under BOOK STORE in the newsletter — see parishOrganizations.

parishOrganizations.value: The parish newsletter's organisation list, with the officers named for each: PARISH COUNCIL (nine, see parishCouncil); STEWARDSHIP — Diane Simeon; CHOIR — nobody named; PHILOPTOCHOS (nine, see philoptochosBoard); BOOK STORE — Jane Kalomatis Moore; FUND RAISING — nobody named; FESTIVAL — nobody named; SUNDAY SCHOOL — Michael Euripides; DANCE — Dr. Judy Marrs, Director; GOYA — Michael Euripides; HOPE/JOY — nobody named.
parishOrganizations.source: The parish newsletter, supplied 2026-08-13 by the volunteer maintaining this repo, and covered by the Parish Council's approval of the roster — see _rosterPermission. The live site's /parish-ministries/ page carries no names at all, checked 2026-08-13, so the Council's word is the only source for these pairings; there is nothing to corroborate them against and no need for one. The HOPE/JOY question below is NOT settled by that approval and stays open.
parishOrganizations.note: TITLES ARE NOT INVENTED. The newsletter gives an explicit title only for Dr. Judy Marrs (Director) and for the Council and Philoptochos officers. Everywhere else it prints an organisation heading and a name underneath and nothing more, so the pages print the bare name and the Ministries hero says what that means: 'Where a name is given, it is the person the parish lists for that ministry.' Nobody is called a director, chair, coordinator or lead who was not called that in the source. Two exceptions where a bare name would have been meaningless in running prose: give.html says stewardship is 'coordinated by' Diane Simeon and bookstore.html says the bookstore is 'kept by' Jane Kalomatis Moore. Both verbs are this project's wording for a newsletter heading plus a name, not the source's, and both are covered by the Council's confirmation that the pairings are right. If either person would put it differently, the sentence is one line each to change. THREE RECONCILIATIONS with the live site's list of eight. (1) CHOIR: settles that a choir exists, which was tagged TODO: verify because the live site has no page for one. The heading 'Choir & Chanters' is now just 'Choir' and the old wording is forbidden in data/site.json — the newsletter says nothing about chanters. (2) HOPE/JOY against the live site's JOY: left alone on every page. HOPE and JOY are separate age groups in the Archdiocese's programme, two parish sources disagree, and no officer is named for either, so there is nothing to choose between. Ask. (3) FUND RAISING and FESTIVAL are organisations in the newsletter with no officer named. Neither got a card on ministries.html: the grid is three columns and nine cells exactly, and the Festival already has both its own page and every 'Greek Festival' link pointing at fredgreek.org by the parish's own instruction (see greekFestival). STEWARDSHIP and BOOK STORE did not get cards either, for a better reason — each already has a whole page of its own, so the name went onto that page instead of into a duplicate card. See ministries for the list itself.

facts._rosterPermission: THE NAMING DECISION, and its approval. 2026-08-13. Twenty-one parishioners are named in this draft: the nine Parish Council members and the nine Philoptochos board members with their offices, plus Diane Simeon, Michael Euripides and Dr. Judy Marrs. Fr. John was already named and is not counted — clergy are published on the live parish site. APPROVED BY THE PARISH COUNCIL, at a meeting before 2026-08-13; relayed on that date by the volunteer maintaining this repo. THE MEETING DATE IS NOT RECORDED HERE because it was not supplied — it is the one gap left in this entry and it is worth filling in, since 'the Council approved it' with no date is exactly the sort of entry that rots. WHAT THE APPROVAL COVERS: both halves. That the names may be published, and that the roster is correct as printed — nine Council members, those four offices, those spellings. That is why no TODO: verify marker remains on any of the twenty-one names, and why parishCouncil, philoptochosBoard and parishOrganizations read CONFIRMED_BY_PARISH rather than UNVERIFIED. Before this approval the markers were doing double duty, standing for an unverified roster AND for absent consent; both reasons are now gone. Do not restore them without a reason of their own. WHAT IT DOES NOT COVER, three things. (1) WHICH COMMITTEE EACH COUNCIL MEMBER LEADS. Not part of the roster and still unknown, so committees.html reads 'Council Member' for every lead and keeps its marker. (2) HOPE/JOY against the live site's JOY — see parishOrganizations; a roster approval says nothing about what a youth group is called. (3) ANY PHOTOGRAPH. Nobody's face is published by this and no photograph in this repository identifies anyone; see assetProvenance._permissionPolicy, which is a separate rule and stands. ONE CAVEAT WORTH KNOWING, not a blocker: the approval as relayed covers all twenty-one names, which includes the nine-member Philoptochos board. The Philoptochos is its own society with its own officers, so strictly that roster is the society's to release rather than the Council's. Nothing here suggests the two disagree, and the parish is one small community where this distinction may be purely formal. Recorded because it costs one sentence, and because the person to ask is the Philoptochos President, whose name is now on the page. WHAT IS PUBLISHED: names and offices only. No personal email address, telephone number, photograph or biography. Council cards show office@ntgoc.org, except the Treasurer's, which shows pctreasurer@ntgoc.org — both verified role addresses, see emails. The Philoptochos cards carry no address at all, and both roster sections say in print that personal addresses are not published and mail should go through the office. TO REVERSE, if a member later objects or the roster changes: the names are in four places — the roster grid on about.html, the ntgocPhiloptochosBoard chunk and the four lead lines on ministries.html, and one sentence each on give.html and bookstore.html. Remove the name, restore the wording the section had before ('Council Member'), re-run npm run chunks, and correct this entry. A single objection does not require dismantling the rest.

greekFestival.note: Design's festival dates and 'two-hour shifts' claim are NOT on the live site — tagged TODO: verify. On 2026-08-08 the parish asked that every "Greek Festival" link go to https://www.fredgreek.org/ rather than to this draft's own festival page, so all 25 of them (top bar and footer on every page, plus the home promo) now point there. festival.html still exists but nothing links to it — a decision for the parish.

externalLinks.note: All present on the live site; the design reproduces them correctly.

orthodoxSaintFinder.source: Named by the project owner on 2026-08-09 as a resource to link from the For Our Parish page.
orthodoxSaintFinder.note: A Cloud of Witnesses / Orthodox Saint Finder. NOT a parish resource, and the page says so in as many words. It is the only third-party Orthodox resource linked from this draft, so it sets a precedent: what else belongs on that list is an editorial question for Fr. John, not one to settle by adding links. The link resolves (npm run links, 2026-08-09).

parishCommunityGroup.note: The 'Join our parish community' button on for-our-parish.html is a placeholder with no link behind it, deliberately. The parish has no private online group — no Facebook group, GroupMe or equivalent has been named. The public Facebook page (facebook.com/ntgoc/) is a different thing and is linked as itself. Do not point this button at the public page to make it look finished.

parishEmailList.note: 'Receive parish updates' is a placeholder for the same reason: no parish email list or sign-up form has been named. The Light newsletter exists and is linked; a list for short-notice news does not. There is also no way for anyone to subscribe themselves to The Light — it is done by asking, and a parishioner reported having to contact several people and finally email Fr. John before being added, months after joining. That is the barrier the sign-up block on welcome.html proposes removing. Until an email system is chosen, newsletter@ntgoc.org is the address that works, and welcome.html prints it next to the proposed form rather than behind it.

stewardshipPledgeForm.note: There is no online stewardship commitment form. give.html carried a dead '2026 stewardship pledge' link (href="#") from the design import until it was replaced by a sentence noting the destination is unconfirmed (see stewardshipDestination), and For Our Parish shows a placeholder rather than repeating that dead link. Giving online (Square) is a separate thing and does work.

volunteerNeeds.note: No rota, sign-up sheet or volunteer-needs system was found or named, so 'Current volunteer needs' is a placeholder. The brief for For Our Parish asked for it only 'if we establish a system for it'.

sundaySchoolResources.note: Sunday School is a confirmed ministry (see `ministries`) and is linked as one. A Sunday School calendar, youth activities listing and parent forms are not published anywhere this draft can see, so For Our Parish names the gap instead of inventing headings for them.

languages.note: Settles a contradiction the draft carried: the design's FAQ said services were 'mostly in English' while the parish-authored Language section said both. Neither was right. Congregational portions — the Creed, the Lord's Prayer — are offered in more than one language. 'mostly in English' is now a forbidden pattern in data/site.json.

communionAndAntidoron.value: Holy Communion is received by Orthodox Christians who are properly prepared to receive the Eucharist. Antidoron is blessed bread anyone may receive, given by the priest as the Liturgy concludes and people leave for the social hall.
communionAndAntidoron.note: The draft said 'baptized and chrismated', which is narrower than what the parish asked for, and mentioned antidoron only in passing inside the Communion paragraph. Antidoron is now its own step in the Sunday timeline, immediately after Communion, so a non-Orthodox visitor reads that they cannot receive the Eucharist and that there is blessed bread for them, in that order.

greeters.value: The parish already has greeters in the narthex on a Sunday morning.
greeters.note: A visitor can be told with confidence that someone will be there. What is NOT current practice, and is presented on visit.html as a proposal: named and pictured greeters ('Faces You Might See'), and a trained Welcome Ministry behind them. No greeter's name or photograph has been invented, and none may be published without that person's own permission.

enteringDuringWorship.value: Visitors are asked to wait quietly in the narthex during key moments of the service — the Little and Great Entrances, the Epistle and the Gospel among them.
enteringDuringWorship.note: Deliberately NOT published as a list for a visitor to memorise. The page says a greeter will guide them, which is both kinder and what actually happens.

dress.value: Dress like you are meeting someone important.
dress.note: Fr. John's own words, and now the foundation of the What Should I Wear section. The draft's paragraph cataloguing what men and women in the parish wear has gone: it read as a dress code and none of it was sourced. Veiling: many women in the parish veil, many do not, and either is comfortable — visitors must never be led to think they need to buy one.

parking.note: There is NO visitor-specific parking and NO overflow arrangement. The draft's Visit page claimed 'additional overflow parking on the grass at feast days and the festival' — invented, and now removed and forbidden in data/site.json.

accessibility.source: Raised with the parish 2026-08-09; no answer yet.
accessibility.designSaid: Step-free entrance on the north side; the hall is reachable by lift.
accessibility.note: Both specifics were unsourced and are removed. The Visit page now asks anyone with a question about getting into the church or the hall to call the office. An accessibility promise that turns out to be wrong strands the person who relied on it, so 'wheelchair', 'step-free', 'accessible entrance' and 'reachable by lift' are forbidden patterns until the parish confirms something.

doorsOpen.source: The design's claim; on no parish source.
doorsOpen.note: Removed from the Visit page's three essentials, where it sat directly beneath the service times and read as confirmed. Replaced by the coffee hour, which is confirmed.

fellowshipMeal.note: The parish calls the post-Liturgy fellowship 'coffee hour'. The draft used 'the Agape Meal' as the primary label on the home, Visit and Parish Life pages — a term the parish does not use for it. It is potluck-style, visitors are welcome, and visitors need bring nothing. It may still be explained in passing as an agape meal, which is why the forbidden pattern is case-sensitive.

bookstore.value: Open every Sunday after Divine Liturgy.
bookstore.note: Stock: Orthodox books, pamphlets, prayer books, icons, prayer ropes, incense, crosses, candles and other devotional items. Visitors are welcome to browse. The draft additionally claimed the table was in the narthex and open during the festival and on feast days — none of that is sourced, and it has been removed.

catechismBooks.value: Fr. John reads two books with those preparing to be received into the Church: 'Know the Faith: A Handbook for Orthodox Christians and Inquirers' (Fr. Michael Shanbour, Ancient Faith Publishing) and 'The Orthodox Church: An Introduction to Eastern Christianity' (Timothy Ware, later Metropolitan Kallistos Ware, Penguin).
catechismBooks.source: Reported by a parish volunteer, 2026-08-10. Not confirmed with Fr. John.
catechismBooks.note: The AUTHORSHIP is settled; what remains unverified is the parish's use of the books. The original report named 'Know the Faith and The Orthodox Church by Timothy Ware', which reads as though Ware wrote both. He did not — Know the Faith is Fr. Michael Shanbour's — and the reporting volunteer confirmed the split attribution on 2026-08-10. Do not let a later edit collapse the two bylines back into one. What is still open is whether Fr. John wants the page to name him at all, or would rather it described the preparation without him. The BOOKS themselves are published works and their titles, authors and publishers are checkable facts; what is unsourced is the claim that this parish uses them. No prices or stock counts have been invented for either — the featured cards carry a Reserve control and no figure. bookstore.html carries the TODO marker.

convertRecommendations.value: Parishioners received into the Church in recent years recommend 'Toolkit for Spiritual Growth: A Practical Guide to Prayer, Fasting, and Almsgiving' (Fr. Evan Armatas, Ancient Faith Publishing).
convertRecommendations.source: Reported by a parish volunteer, 2026-08-10. Not confirmed with Fr. John.
convertRecommendations.note: One title was supplied and one title is shown. Nothing was added to make the section look fuller — the second cell of the grid is a labelled proposal saying the list is short on purpose, which is the same treatment the greeter portraits and the Parish Life gallery get. Recommendations are published WITHOUT names, per the parish's photography and permission position: see photographyPolicy. Open questions for Fr. John: whether the parish is content to publish a reading list it has not vetted, and how a parishioner adds to it.

sundaySchool.value: During the school year, parish children attending Sunday School leave for class after Holy Communion has been served, and remain in class until coffee hour.
sundaySchool.note: Whether a VISITING child may join a class the same day is NOT settled — visiting parents are told to ask a greeter, and no answer is invented. Grade and age ranges are unsourced: the draft's 'ages 4 through high school', 'grades 7-12' and 'grades 3-6' have been removed from the home page and the Ministries page and must not come back.

newsletter.note: The frequency is now stated on newsletter.html and in the For Our Parish resource directory. The copy deadline and the editor remain unknown. Distribution is now recorded separately under weeklyBulletin below: The Light itself is emailed monthly as a PDF, with no per-issue web archive, so no issue URL has been invented or linked.

weeklyBulletin.value: Weekly bulletins are posted at https://bulletinbuilder.org/ntgoc/. Monthly newsletter ("The Light") issues are emailed as a link to a PDF, one link per email — there is no stable public URL for a given issue, so no individual issue is linked from the site.
weeklyBulletin.source: Named directly by the project owner (Thomas), 2026-08-13.
weeklyBulletin.note: The bulletinbuilder.org page was checked and does show a current weekly Nativity of the Theotokos bulletin. newsletter.html links to it from the 'Back issues' section, in place of the six dead year-span placeholders' old invitation to 'send the issues' — that invitation is now answered. Whether the six year spans should eventually become a real by-year archive, and whether monthly PDFs would ever be gathered into one, is still open; nothing has been invented to fill that gap.

stewardshipDestination.note: The parish has stewardship information, but the destination for the annual pledge on the redesigned site is not known. give.html and for-our-parish.html carry a labelled placeholder saying so. The two bare href="#" buttons that sat among three live ones on give.html are gone: one is now the verified family-registration form, the other is a sentence. Online giving, memorial donations, building projects and family registration all have verified URLs (see externalLinks).

visitorFollowUp.value: The parish collects no visitor information and has no follow-up of any kind.
visitorFollowUp.note: Shown on visit.html as a PROPOSAL, because the gap is the point. The form there is inert: no action, no method, every field disabled, no submit handler and no JavaScript. Nothing is collected or transmitted. Whether the parish should collect anything at all is Fr. John's decision, not this draft's. welcome.html (added 2026-08-10) proposes the same thing from the other end of a visit and carries three separate forms — a question, a survey and a mailing-list sign-up. Those three ARE interactive, so that the Council can see the exchange a visitor would have, but none of them has a handler: the submit is intercepted in assets/js/ntgoc-enhance.js, nothing is transmitted or stored, and each block says so and prints the parish address that works today.

visitorSurvey.note: No visitor survey of any kind is run today, and there is nowhere for answers to go. The survey on welcome.html is a proposal. Its field names — firstVisit, greeted, foundBook, comfortableAsking, knewCoffeeHour, introduced, confusedBy, couldImprove, wantToKnowMore, contactMe — are fixed now so that the shape of any future summary does not depend on whichever form tool is eventually chosen. No summary or reporting screen has been built, and none should be until the parish decides it wants the survey at all.

welcomePageDoctrinalContent.value: The nineteen explanations on welcome.html, checked against Archdiocese sources.
welcomePageDoctrinalContent.source: Checked 2026-08-10 against the Archdiocese's Our Faith content (mirrored at nativity.va.goarch.org/our-faith/worship, /liturgy, /house_of_god), the parish's own FAQ at nativity.va.goarch.org/about-us/faq, and goarch.org articles on the Sign of the Cross, Kyrie Eleison, the Nativity of the Theotokos, and visiting an Orthodox church.
welcomePageDoctrinalContent.note: Confirmed: the Sign of the Cross finger positions; Kyrie Eleison and the eleos/olive-oil root, which is the Archdiocese's own gloss and not a homiletic flourish; Theotokos and the Council of Ephesus in 431; the feast on 8 September; the Little and Great Entrances; antidoron open to all including non-Orthodox; Communion for Orthodox Christians only; icons venerated and not worshipped; standing as the preferred posture. Corrected four things: the Divine Liturgy was described as prayed in substantially its present form for sixteen centuries, which contradicts the Archdiocese's account that its core is apostolic and its framework settled by about the ninth century; the congregation was said to stand for the anaphora, when kneeling at the consecration is expressly permitted; the iconostasis description was vague where the Archdiocese is specific (right: Christ and St. John the Baptist; left: the Theotokos and the church's patron); and 'the shortest prayer the Church prays' was an unsourced superlative. None of this replaces Fr. John reading the page.
welcomePageDoctrinalContent.alsoFound: The parish's own live FAQ page states the Communion practice, the invitation to non-Orthodox to receive antidoron, and 'there is often as much Greek as English in the service'. All three were previously recorded here as confirmed only by direct conversation with the parish; they now have a published parish source as well.

visitorSeriesVideos.value: Three additional videos in the Frederica Mathewes-Green orientation series, embedded on visit.html: 'An Overview of the Orthodox Divine Liturgy' (YouTube ID XDUMf7oFt2s), 'The Sign of the Cross, Icons, and Tradition in the Orthodox Church' (derjqczKV5E), and 'A Little More About the Orthodox Worship Space' (0Ye_QDBA5Ps).
visitorSeriesVideos.source: IDs found by searching video titles on 2026-08-08. Not one of the three has been played to confirm it is the video its title and embed claim.
visitorSeriesVideos.note: 2026-08-11 audit: each embed already carried a TODO: verify HTML comment naming the risk, but none had a matching entry here. The risk is concrete: a wrong video ID silently embeds the wrong episode (or someone else's video) under the parish's page. Play all three and confirm title, content and speaker before the markers come off. The first video in the same series ('An Introduction to the Orthodox Worship Space', YimgCkBbH7c) is NOT included in this entry — it carries no TODO: verify marker on the page and was not flagged by the audit.

liturgicalPrayerTexts.value: The English text of the Nicene Creed and the Lord's Prayer printed on visit.html, in the 'Words you may begin to recognise' section.
liturgicalPrayerTexts.source: Standard Archdiocese-family English wording, reproduced from memory/reference rather than transcribed from the parish's own Divine Liturgy book.
liturgicalPrayerTexts.note: 2026-08-11 audit: both blocks already carried a TODO: verify HTML comment (Creed at visit.html, and the Lord's Prayer immediately below it, including whether the priest concludes with the doxology here) but neither had a matching entry here. Both need to be checked word for word against the translation actually printed in this parish's pew book before publishing without the marker — Orthodox parishes in the English-speaking world do not all use identical translations.

welcomeGoarchLinks.value: Four goarch.org links on welcome.html: 'Kyrie Eleison, on goarch.org' (https://www.goarch.org/-/kyrie-eleison-lord-have-mercy), the Archdiocese's Nativity of the Theotokos feast page (https://www.goarch.org/nativity-theotokos), 'The true nature of fasting' (https://www.goarch.org/-/the-true-nature-of-fasting), and 'What to expect when visiting an Orthodox Christian church' (https://www.goarch.org/-/what-to-expect-when-visiting-an-orthodox-christian-church).
welcomeGoarchLinks.source: URLs found by search on 2026-08-10; each destination page's content was not independently confirmed to match its linked description.
welcomeGoarchLinks.note: 2026-08-11 audit: all four already carried a TODO: verify HTML comment on welcome.html noting that goarch.org returns 403 to automated requests, so `npm run links` cannot check them — they must be opened by hand. None had a matching entry here. This entry does not cover the several `nativity.va.goarch.org` (the parish's own site) links elsewhere on welcome.html and other pages, which are a different domain and were not flagged by the audit.

committeeStructure.value: Six standing Parish Council committees, each with a stated mandate: Building and Grounds / Facilities; Worship / Liturgical; Fellowship / Hospitality; Education / Catechesis; Youth and Family; Fundraising and Events.
committeeStructure.source: Carried over from the Get Involved / Committees brief; not confirmed against a parish source. No committees page exists on the live parish site.
committeeStructure.note: 2026-08-11 audit: committees.html had TODO: verify markers only on the placeholder lead names (see `parishCouncil`) and on the hero sentence's committee count — nothing recorded the committee list or descriptions themselves, which is everything else on the page. Both the hero's 'six standing committees' and each committee's mandate paragraph now carry TODO: verify markers pointing at this entry. If the parish's actual committee structure differs — a different count, different names, or a different division of responsibilities — this whole section needs rewriting, not just the leads.

pewCard.value: An 'Understanding the Divine Liturgy' pew card and a physical Welcome Packet.
pewCard.source: Described in the brief for welcome.html, 2026-08-10; not confirmed with the parish office.
pewCard.note: welcome.html is written as the page a QR code on that card and in that packet would lead to. Neither the card, the packet nor any QR code has been seen by this project, and no wording from the printed card has been reproduced. The card's entry on welcome.html links to the Visit page's 'Sunday morning, step by step' — the nearest thing that exists on this site — rather than to a guide that has not been written.

touchingVestmentsAtGreatEntrance.value: Reaching out to touch the priest's vestment as he passes with the gifts at the Great Entrance.
touchingVestmentsAtGreatEntrance.source: Reported by a parishioner, 2026-08-10. The practice itself is well attested and is described in the same terms by other parishes of the Archdiocese, which trace it to Matthew 9:20-22 — the woman healed by touching the hem of Christ's garment — and add the etiquette: do not step into the procession, do not tug at the vestments, do not push anyone aside.
touchingVestmentsAtGreatEntrance.note: It is expressly NOT a universal Orthodox practice; it is most common among Greek and Middle Eastern Christians and varies parish by parish. The card on welcome.html is therefore written conditionally — 'if you saw this' — rather than telling a visitor they will have seen it, and carries a TODO: verify. Fr. John should confirm it is the habit here before the marker comes off.

childrenActivityBoxes.value: Children's activity boxes are available outside the parish bookstore.
childrenActivityBoxes.source: Reported by a parishioner in the brief for welcome.html, 2026-08-10.
childrenActivityBoxes.note: Stated on welcome.html with a TODO: verify marker. Plausible and specific, but it comes from one parishioner rather than the parish office, and a visitor sent to look for something that is not there is exactly the small failure this page exists to catch. Confirm the boxes exist and where they are kept before the marker is removed.

parishCommunity.value: There is no private parish Facebook group, Discord, GroupMe or other parish chat, and no parish mailing list.
parishCommunity.note: for-our-parish.html shows both as proposals with inert <span> buttons rather than links, so there is nothing to click through to a destination that does not exist.

photographyPolicy.value: There is no formal parish photography or permission policy.
photographyPolicy.note: Until there is one, the draft applies the strictest reading: no identifiable parishioner or child is published to fill a placeholder, the Parish Life gallery ships as labelled empty frames, and the greeter portraits stay empty. Developing a policy is a recommendation for a future phase.

liturgicalOfferings.value: What the parish wants parishioners to bring for prosphora, altar wine, olive oil and flowers — the kind, the quantity, when, and where to leave it.
liturgicalOfferings.source: Nothing. Not on the live parish site, not supplied in any brief, and not asked of the parish yet.
liturgicalOfferings.note: This is the section of get-involved.html most likely to be filled in by accident. 'A good-quality dry red wine' and 'extra virgin olive oil' are what most parishes use, and writing either one would produce a page of instructions this project invented, printed under the parish's name, that a parishioner would follow to the shop. Every row on all four cards therefore reads 'To be confirmed by the parish' and carries a TODO: verify marker. They are local decisions and Fr. John and Presbytera make them. Filling one in is a two-minute job once the answer exists; guessing it wastes somebody's money and hands the priest a problem on a Sunday morning.

prosphoraTeaching.value: Presbytera teaches prosphora-baking classes covering the parish's own practice, and bakers join a rotation after being taught.
prosphoraTeaching.source: Described in the Get Involved brief, 2026-08-11. Nothing on the live parish site; see also prosphoraClass, reported separately on 2026-08-10 for traditions.html.
prosphoraTeaching.note: Two claims in one sentence, and the second is about a person. That the parish runs the classes is unconfirmed. That PRESBYTERA teaches them is a statement of a named individual's role — no surname is printed, but 'Presbytera' identifies exactly one person in this parish, so her agreement to be named is part of what has to be confirmed, not only the fact. Rendered with a TODO: verify marker on get-involved.html and on traditions.html. If she would rather not be named, the sentence works as 'the parish offers prosphora-baking classes' with no loss.

prosphoraRotation.value: An approved rotation of bakers, with a published schedule of who bakes on which Sunday.
prosphoraRotation.source: Proposed in the Get Involved brief, 2026-08-11.
prosphoraRotation.note: Built as a table with column headings and no rows. A specimen row would do two damaging things at once: it would be read as the real rota, and it would publish a parishioner's name against a date. Two design decisions are deliberate and should survive review — the rotation is ASKED ABOUT rather than joined, because an open sign-up routes around whatever teaching the parish requires first; and the schedule, when it exists, is for approved bakers to coordinate with, not a public directory. How approval is granted is Fr. John and Presbytera's to decide and is recorded nowhere yet.

churchPreparation.value: When the church is decorated for the Nativity, for Holy Week and for the feasts; who does it now; what help and what materials are wanted; and which tasks a parishioner may do.
churchPreparation.source: Nothing. The Get Involved brief asks for the section; none of the particulars was supplied.
churchPreparation.note: The Prepare & Beautify section states the general shape of the work and nothing else. Every date, contact and requirement reads 'To be confirmed by the parish'. One question matters more than the rest and is not this project's to answer: which of these tasks are open to any parishioner and which are arranged with Father because they happen inside the church or around things set apart for worship. The page says that distinction exists rather than drawing it.

hosting.cms: Evolution CMS (EVO), Greek Orthodox Archdiocese Department of Internet Ministries
notes: custom.css already exists at the template asset root — strong evidence that additional custom stylesheets CAN be added. Confirm with DIM before relying on it.
css-vars-ponyfill is loaded, which implies the template already expects CSS custom properties and that legacy-browser support was a concern. Our --ntgoc-* tokens should be safe.
Bootstrap 4.1.3 styles bare element selectors (h1-h6, p, a, ul). components.css must set those properties explicitly on .ntgoc-* classes rather than relying on inheritance.
hosting.evoVersionNote: Reported as 'pretty sure 1.4.x' by the project owner, 2026-08-08. Not verified against the manager's About screen or DIM. It matters: the chunk-call syntax this project relies on ({{chunkName}}, [~id~], [*tv*]) is the Evolution 1.x family. Evolution 3.x changes template/element handling, so if it turns out to be 3.x the IMPORT.md syntax needs rechecking. Confirm in the manager footer or Help -> About before importing.

cmsMajorVersion.source: Inference, 2026-08-09: the parish install was compared against a local Evolution CMS 1.4.18 and a local 3.5.7 running side by side (tools/evo-sandbox), and it matches the 1.4 manager. NOT read from Help -> About or confirmed by the Department of Internet Ministries.
cmsMajorVersion.note: Strong evidence, but still inference — so IMPORT.md's "reported as 1.4.x, but not confirmed" caveat stands, and the About screen should still be checked before an import. What this does settle is that IMPORT.md is written against the right syntax. Worth recording either way: the tag syntax is identical in both versions — 3.5.7 still implements {{ }}, [* *], [( )] and [~ ~] — so the chunks import unmodified even if the version turns out to be 3.x. The difference between the versions is how the manager presents Elements, not how pages parse.

assetProvenance._permissionPolicy: Set by the parish 2026-08-13: a photograph the parish has ALREADY PUBLISHED ITSELF — on nativity.va.goarch.org, in its Flickr-backed photo gallery, or on its social media — carries the permission of the people in it. The parish obtained that when it published. Nothing further is needed for those, and the entries below no longer flag them. THIS DOES NOT REACH PHOTOGRAPHS THE PARISH NEVER PUBLISHED. A private photograph, however freely given by whoever took it, still needs the agreement of the people in it — owning a photograph and having the agreement of the person in it are two different things. Two files are still outstanding on that basis: clergy-fr-john.jpg and holy-week-service.jpg. See each. Note also that permission to appear is not permission to be named, and this policy does not decide the naming question either way. AMENDED 2026-08-13: it is no longer true that no names are published in this repository. Twenty-one parishioners are named across about.html, ministries.html, give.html and bookstore.html, approved by the Parish Council — that approval covers names only and reaches no photograph; see facts._rosterPermission. Nobody in any photograph here is identified, which is what this policy is about, and that still stands.
